text:
incident-bot: Paging: P1 — elevated 5xx rate detected for Peregrine VPC (dedicated-pool-3) on /generate endpoint. Condition: 5xx_rate > 4% over 5m. Runbook: /runbooks/pool-5xx
mia (oncall): Ack. Joining bridge now. Collecting traces and logs.
raj (eng-runtime): Looking at runtime logs — repeated KV cache misses and batching fallbacks from nvidia-rt-02..04. Seeing memory pressure spikes coincident with model-variant switch.
elena (support): Peregrine ops reported increased errors and latency at ~15:12 UTC, they started retrying upstream. They mentioned heavy analytics job kicked off.
mia (oncall): Can we confirm if this is a tenant-local issue or pool-wide noisy neighbor?
raj (eng-runtime): Querying tenant labels... looks like tenant peregrine-analytics accounts for 86% of active tokens on the pool. Other tenants' metrics flat. Suggest isolating that tenant.
mia (oncall): Agreed. Plan: evict peregrine-analytics from dedicated-pool-3 -> route to dedicated-burst-1. Prep notification to customer.
raj (eng-runtime): Running eviction command now:
```
redwoodctl pool evict --pool dedicated-pool-3 --tenant peregrine-analytics --reason "live mitigation: cache thrash" --keep-keys false
```
sam (acct-exec): Heads up — moving tenant will impact throughput for that workload temporarily. I'll let Peregrine AE know and prep a short customer note.
tori (customer-success): Drafting status update: "We detected a noisy workload in your VPC that impacted other requests. We're migrating that workload to a dedicated burst pool to restore performance. Minimal rolling disruption expected." Will post asap.
ops-bot: Action: tenant eviction started. migration-job=873 ETA ~3m. Link: https://ops.redwood/jobs/873
raj (eng-runtime): Migration in progress. Observability: 5xxs dropping from 4.6% -> 0.9% in last 2m, tail latency improving.
elena (support): Peregrine confirms partial restoration on their side. Their ops says errors near-zero after migration.
mia (oncall): Good. Keeping the bridge open for monitoring for 30m. Next: collect impact window (start/end), count affected tokens, and capture timelines for RCA.
tori (customer-success): I'll compile a customer-facing timeline and an exec summary draft. Need final impact numbers for credits.
raj (eng-runtime): Initial root cause hypothesis: high-rate analytics job caused KV cache thrash, which increased batching contention and triggered transient 5xxs on the serving runtime. Contributing factor: a model variant fallback increased memory churn. Draft RCA bullet: "Noisy tenant (peregrine-analytics) caused KV cache thrash -> batching failures -> elevated 5xxs for pool. Mitigated by tenant eviction and migration to dedicated burst capacity."
mia (oncall): Proposed remediations: 1) per-tenant QPS limits, 2) circuit-breaker for KV cache thrash patterns, 3) telemetry to detect cache-eviction storms and auto-isolate noisy tenants. Assign owners.
raj (eng-runtime): I'll own circuit-breaker + telemetry PR (ENG-6791). ETA: EOD for initial instrumentation, follow-up week for hard limits.
elena (support): For credits & SLA impact we need: token_count_affected, time_window (15:12 -> 15:20 UTC), and estimated customer errors.
harry (finance): I'll calculate provisional credit once you post token/time numbers — expect estimate in 24h. Please tag FIN-88 when ready.
sam (acct-exec): Also prepping an exec one-pager for Peregrine leadership — want a clear mitigation timeline and next steps. Tori will review.
tori (customer-success): I'll share the RCA draft and suggested credit proposal to Peregrine contact and legal. Goal: formal RCA within 48h, credit proposal within 72h. @peregrine-ops FYI.
ops-bot: Bridge closed. Final status: mitigation successful. Follow-ups created: ENG-6791 (circuit-breaker & telemetry), CS-312 (customer comms & exec summary), FIN-88 (credit calc).
mia (oncall): Closing thread. Thanks everyone — good collaboration. :thumbsup:
